title: Move Buttonhole
content: ### Objective Move buttonholes as desired. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Window Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button ### Operation #### Move Buttonholes with Click-and-Drag 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Window Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button 2. Click and drag the buttonholes to the desired location on either of 2D or 3D Pattern. → The selected buttonholes are now being moved accordingly. ※ Note: Move multiple buttonholes at once by selecting them in the 2D window (ver2.4.0). #### Move Buttonholes with Distance Input (ver2.5.0) 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Window Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button 2. While click-and-dragging the buttonholes with left-click mouse button, click right-click mouse button in either of 2D or 3D window. →The Moving Distance window appears. 3. Enter desired value in the menu. Distance Moved | Sets the moved distance of the buttonhole from its original location. ---|--- Position | Sets the position of the center of the buttonhole from the left/right/top/bottom of the pattern outline. 4. Click OK. → The buttonholes are now being moved according to the input value. ※ Note: Buttonholes can only be moved within the boundaries of the Pattern.
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions on how to move buttonholes within a pattern using click-and-drag or distance input methods in a 2D or 3D design interface.

title: Trim Properties (ver. 2024.0)
content: ### Objective Set the properties of a Trim. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Trim ### Operation 1. Open trim window by going to Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Trim 2. Select the Trim Style. →The Trim properties will display in Property Editor. **Trim properties** Properties | Description ---|--- Information | Name | You can rename the trim. Surface | Skin Offset | Adjusts the spacing between objects and trim. Static Friction | This is the coefficient of friction between the garment and the accessories when the garment is stationary. Kinetic Friction | It refers to the coefficient of friction between the garment and its accessories in situations where the garment needs to move. Specification | Scale (local) | X (mm) | Scales along the X-axis. Y (mm) | Scales along the Y-axis. Z (mm) | Scales along the Z-axis. Lock Aspect Ratio | Fix the default proportions of the trim. Weight | Set the weight of the trim. Collision (ver. 11) | Sets whether the accessory should collide. You can only set collision handling for accessories that are not attached to a garment. Collision Thickness | Sets the thickness of the collision with the clothing. The higher the thickness value, the wider the simulated gap with the garment. Material (selected) | Set the [Material](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358364198425) of the trims Miscellaneous | Mesh type | This indicates the type of mesh. Element Count | Indicates the number of points in the mesh. Polygon Optimization | Count | Sets the number of polygons. Plane | Applied in the form of a texture when the Plane is activated. Count cannot be set on Plane activation. ※Note: When you select a Trim, the properties of that object appear in the Property Editor window. (ver. 2024.1 and bellow)
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for setting and adjusting the properties of a Trim in the software, including options for styling, scaling, friction, and collision settings.

title: Requesting Network Software License activation - First Time installation
content: **[Software License Key for Network Offline] Generate a C2V for First Time Installation for Window** In order to request Network Offline License activation with a Software License key, please follow the instruction below. **1\. Install a Run-time Environment on your Windows license server.** Step 1. Download the driver from the link here (**[HASP Driver Download Link](https://s3.amazonaws.com/s3.md.web.upload/newmdweb/helpcenter/installer/haspdinst_8_31+\(2\).exe)**). Step 2. Press 'Windows Start Button + Run (R)' and then enter "CMD" in the text field to open the Command Prompt window. (Example) ![first_time_installation_EN_.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/51987431843865) Step 3. Drag the downloaded haspdinst.exe file and put it on the CMD window to automatically register the corresponding path as shown underlined below. Enter "-i" behind the automatically entered path and press 'Enter' on the keyboard to install. (Example)** ** ![0.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/51987431846297) Step 4. In a web browser, navigate to **<http://localhost:1947>** and check to see if the following screen appears to verify the HASP Driver has been successfully installed. If the following screen appears, then the installation has been successful. ![1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/51987431849241) * If an error message pops up, please refer to the troubleshooting manual for “Sentinel HASP Driver Errors on Windows part”. **[Link to the Manual](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358254274585)** **2\. After HASP Driver installation completes, download the RUS ****(attachment at the bottom of this post) and generate a C2V file.** *We recommend that you remove any previously owned MD hardware dongle keys from your network before generating a C2V file to avoid conflicts. **You would need to select the second option on RUS**“Installation of new protection key”** to successfully create a C2V file.** ** ![mceclip0.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/51987415862937) 3\. Submit your C2V file through [**this page**](https://marvelousdesigner.com/teamconsole/keyupdate/1) (logging in with your Company ID is required). If you experience any difficulties, please contact us via support@marvelousdesigner.com **[Applying a V2C on the server]** 1\. Download the V2C file sent from Marvelous Designer Support Team. 2\. Click on the link below to access the ACC Page, then select “Update/Attach” in Options on the left. **(Click here to link[ACC Page](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html))** **![2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/51987431853721)** 3\. Click “Choose File” to find and select the downloaded V2C file. ![3.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/51987431856153) 4\. Click “Apply File”. 5\. If the update is successful, the following message will be printed. ![5.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/51987415867289) **[Double checking an updated License Key]** If the License Key Update process is successfully completed, you will be able to double check by following the steps below. 1\. Open a web browser and navigate to the **[ACC Page](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html)** **2\. Click Features once you see the key info.** ![6.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/51987415867929) 3\. Make sure the number in the red box has been changed to correctly. ![7.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/51987431859609)
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions for generating a C2V file for first-time installation of a network offline license using a software license key on a Windows server.

title: Show 2D Measurements
content: ### Objective Show or hide 2D measurements on 2D Patterns (ver2.5.0). ※Note: * All 2D measurements are created based on the Internal Shapes/Lines drawn on Patterns. * All 2D measurements are deactivated by default. In order to activate them, please navigate to the Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurements. Then, choose either the To Center or the To Outline option to expand each option's child menu. Toggle on following options to activate the 2D measurements. When you choose To Center, Marvelous Designer calculates the distances from the Pattern outline to the center of the Internal Shapes/Lines. On the other hand, when you choose To Outline, Marvelous Designer calculates the distances from the Pattern outline to the outline of the Internal Shapes/Lines. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Show 2D Measurements Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Show 2D Measurements ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Show 2D Measurements Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Show 2D Measurements →The 2D measurements show or disappear from the 2D window.
content_description: This web page provides instructions on how to activate and display 2D measurements on patterns in Marvelous Designer, allowing users to analyze distances from internal shapes to pattern outlines.

title: AVATAR CREATING MEASUREMENT: Edit Measurement
content: ### Objective Edit avatar measurements. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Measure Tab ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Measure Tab → The list of avatar measurements created on the active Avatar appears. 2. Click on the measurement to see or edit its properties. Name | Rename the measurement. | Basic Length | Check the measurement's basic length. ---|---|---|--- Measurement Type | Change the measurement type. | Surface Length | Check the surface length of the measurement. Measurement Information | Check the measurement's information. | Show | Show or hide the selected measurement.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide users with an intuitive interface for editing and managing avatar measurements within the Avatar Editor.

title: OBJ TRIM: Transform OBJ Trims
content: ### Objective Transform OBJ files loaded as trim as needed. ### Location #### Via the Scale Gizmo Load OBJ as Trim ▶ Scale #### Via the Property Editor Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Select/Move 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ### Operation #### Via the Scale Gizmo 1. Load an OBJ. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Load OBJ as Trim ▶ Scale 3. Click and drag on the x,y, or z-axis to transform the OBJ. Axis | Description ---|--- X-Axis | The red axis of the Gizmo. Click and drag the x-axis to transform the OBJ trim along its x-axis. Y-Axis | The yellow-green axis of the Gizmo. Click and drag the y-axis to transform the OBJ trim along its y-axis. Z-Axis | The blue axis of the Gizmo. Click and drag the z-axis to transform the OBJ along its z-axis. Square | The yellow square located in the center of the Scale Gizmo. Click and drag the square to transform the OBJ trim, while maintaining its x, y, and z ratio. → The OBJ is transformed. 4. When the OBJ transformation is complete, click the Scale button again. → The Gizmo used for moving and rotating OBJs appears. #### Via the Property Editor 1. Load an OBJ. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Select/Move 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move 3. Select the OBJ to be transformed. → The properties of the OBJ appear in the Property Editor. 4. Find the Scale option. 5. Enter the desired value for the below options. Option | Description ---|--- X-Axis | Enter the desired x-axis value. Y-Axis | Enter the desired y-axis value. Z-Axis | Enter the desired z-axis value. Maintain Ratio | Toggle this option on to adjust an OBJ while maintaining its x, y, and z ratio.
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions on how to transform OBJ files by scaling them using the Scale Gizmo or the Property Editor in a 3D design environment.

title: Avatar Measure (above ver 10)
content: ### Objective Measure the circumference, length and height of the Avatar. Two methods are provided. Either based on the protruding part of the avatar or based on the surface of the curvature. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Measurement 3D Toolbar ▶ Click and hold down the Basic Circumference Measure ### Operation **Basic/Surface Circumference Measure.** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click the starting point to be measured and click the second point in the desired direction. → A Basic/Surface Circumference measure is displayed. 3. Click once more when it is in the target shape. → A Basic/Surface Circumference measure is created and the length is displayed. **Basic/Surface/Linear Measure** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click the start point to be measured and double-click the end point. → A Basic/Surface/Linear Tape Measure is created and its length is displayed. → A Linear Measure runs through the Avatar by connecting the start and end points in a straight line. **Height Measure** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click the point to be measured. → A Height Measure that runs vertically from the clicked point to the ground is created and the length is displayed. ※ Note: * Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to create vertical/horizontal/45˚ tilt. * Use Attach to Measure tool to attach the pattern outline or Internal Line to the Avatar Measure. ## Attach to Measure (Avatar) ### Objective Attach avatar tapes to internal or external seam/pattern lines. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Measurement ▶ Attach to Measure (Avatar) 3D Toolbar ▶ Click and hold down the Edit Measure (Avatar) ▶ Attach to Measure (Avatar) ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2. In the 3D window, select seam or pattern line to attach to avatar tape. → Pattern with the selected line becomes transparent and the selected line gets highlighted in red. 3. Select avatar tape to be attached. → Once it is selected, the pattern becomes normal, the attached seam or pattern line and the avatar tape becomes in red. 4. To detach avatar tape from seam or pattern line, click on Attach to Avatar Tape tool again, and press 'Delete' on keyboard. ## Edit Measure (Avatar) Option ### Objective Show or hide the length indicated on the Tape Measure ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Measure (Avatar) ### Operation Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Right-click on the Tape Measure and set the options below. Delete Measure | Delete the Tape Measure ---|--- Duplicate to Symmetric Position (ver 11) | Duplicate the tape measure to the symmetrical position of the avatar. Show/ Show All Length | The selected tape measure or the length of the entire tape measure is shown or hidden.
content_description: This webpage provides detailed instructions for measuring the dimensions of an avatar using various methods, including circumference, length, height, and attaching measurement tapes to seams or pattern lines.

title: Zoom Extents All (2D)
content: ### Objective Set the view in the 2D window to reveal all patterns or center the 2D view to the center of the 2D grid. ### Location Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ Zoom Extents All ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ Zoom Extents All → The 2D view is adjusted to reveal all existing 2D Patterns, if any, or resets the view to the center of the 2D window.
content_description: This webpage provides instructions for using the "Zoom Extents All" feature in the 2D window to either display all existing patterns or center the view within the grid.

title: Copy/Paste Button
content: ### Objective Copy and paste multiple buttons with keeping the interval space evenly or to Symmetric Patterns. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button ### Operation #### Copy/Paste Button 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button 2. Right click on an existing button, then select Copy (Ctrl+C). 3. Right click the same button again, then select Paste (Ctrl+V). 4. Click on a desired place to locate the copy of the button. #### Input Interval/Number/Position to Copy/Paste Button 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button 2. Right click on an existing button, then select Copy (Ctrl+C). 3. Right click the same button again, then select Paste (Ctrl+V). 4. Right click on a desired place to locate the copy of the button. →The Paste window appears. 5. Input desired value for Interval, Number of Buttons, and Position. Interval | Sets the distance between buttons. ---|--- Number of Buttons/Buttonholes | Sets the number of buttons to copy/paste. Position | Sets the position of the center of the copied button/buttonhole from the left/right/top/bottom of the pattern outline (ver2.5.0). 6. Click OK. → The buttons are now being created and applied accordingly. #### Duplicate Button to Symmetric Pattern 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button 2. Select a button to duplicate. → The selected button is now being highlighted in yellow color. 3. Right click on the selected button. → Pop-up menu appears. 4. Select Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern from the menu. → The selected button is now being duplicated at the same level.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for efficiently copying, pasting, and arranging buttons with even intervals or in symmetric patterns within your project.

title: 3D File (OBJ) Import/Export
content: ### OBJ Import/Export ### Objective An OBJ file is used when saving Scene and Props that organize Avatar and surrounding environment. If the OBJ type is an Avatar, the OBJ file is able to wear Garments but if it is a Trim, the Garment passes through it as it does not recognize it as an object. For detailed instruction on how to use OBJ files as Trims, refer to Load As Trim. Furthermore, OBJ files with the same Mesh structure (net-shaped structure expresses 3D objects) is able to be "Morphed" to change Avatar's appearance. “Morphing” refers to slowly changing the appearance of one object into another, and this function can be used to change Avatar's poses or body type. This function is useful when changing Poses of an Avatar in Garments. For detailed instruction, refer to Load as Morph Target. Garments made with Marvelous Designer are able to be formatted/imported in *.obj file and they are compatible with other 3D software. When exporting Garments in an *.obj file, a *.mtl file is also created, and this *.mtl file saves material information of the Garment. ### Location #### OBJ Import Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ #### Additional OBJ Import Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import (Add) ▶ OBJ #### OBJ Export Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ OBJ #### Selected OBJ Export Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ OBJ (Selected) ### Operation #### OBJ Import 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ → Open File window appears. 2. Select a file and click OK. → Import OBJ window appears. 3. Set details and click OK. ※ Note: #### OBJ Import Detail Settings Object Type | Load as Avatar | Imports an object as an avatar and replaces it with the original avatar. Add Arrangement Points &BVs: Turn on this option to generate Bounding Volumes and Arrangement Points fit to the imported OBJ (ver4.2.0). ※Note: This option works properly only when imported OBJ is either in T or A pose and below error message appears when this function cannot be applied properly. "Arrangement Points were not fitted to the avatar. The avatar must be in a T-pose or A-pose." ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438250166297) ---|---|--- Load as Trim | Due to nonfunctional collision detection, objects pass through garments (ver3.0.0). Load as Garment | Import an object as a 3D Garment. Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map: Toggle on this option to generate Patterns based on UV Map information (ver4.2.0). Load as Morph Target | Morphs the original object into the object designated as the Morph Target. Enter the Transition Frame Count. The higher the frame count, the slower the morphing process. Scale | Manually enters values or selects the desired unit. Axis Conversion | Changes the directions of each axis of an object. When the OBJ is placed below the ground, please toggle on Align Bottom to Ground option to pull up the OBJ file above the ground (ver4.2.0). ※ Note: Load as Garment - Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map #### OBJ Additional Import 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import (Add) ▶ OBJ → The Add File window appears. 2. Set details and click OK. #### OBJ Export 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ OBJ (Selected) → Save File window appears. 2. Select desired location to store, and click Save. → Export OBJ window appears. 3. Set details and click OK. ※ Note: #### OBJ Export Detail Settings Object | Select All Patterns: Select/Deselect all Patterns. Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right (ver2.2.0). ※ Note: If OBJ(Selected) is utilized, selected Patterns are being checked in the 3D and 2D window. Select All Avatars: Select/Deselect all Avatars/Objects. Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right (ver2.2.0). Select All Graphics/Top-stitches: Select/Deselect all Graphics/Top-stitches. Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right (ver2.2.0). ---|--- #### Single Object Exports selected object as a single object. | #### Multiple Objects Exports selected object as multiple objects. #### Unweld Exports Vertex(points of mesh) of sewn pattern parts as multiple objects. | #### Weld Combines Vertex (points of mesh) of sewn pattern parts together as one point. Weld Selected Pattern: Weld sewing-lines of selected patterns. #### Thin Ensures thickness is not exported to Geometry even if the value is increased beforehand. | #### Thick Exports thickness value to Geometry. ※ Note: Thickness is available to be exported when pattern's mesh is Quad (ver2.3.0). Combined UV Coordinates: Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit to UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1. ※Note: Unified Texture (ver3.1.0). Export multiple layers of texture information as a single UV texture information. | Image File | Designate file saving path and file name. Add numbers behind the file name as below: ‘File Name_0’, ‘File Name_1’. ---|--- Texture Size | Width and Height will be saved in a fixed ratio. Allowance: 100 ~ 10000 Pixel Fill Texture Seams | Expands the scope of the texture having its boundary line as the standard. Allowance: 0 ~ 15 mm When you type in values, preview will show in the 2D Window. Include Internal Shape: Includes internal line and/or shape information in export (ver2.3.0). Scale | Adjusts scale of file being exported when a value is entered or desired unit from 'Unit in file to import' is selected. Axis Conversion | Changes directions of object's each axis. File | Save with Texture File (*.zip): Exports .obj file, .mtl file, and texture images used in the garment as one compressed file when exporting animation. Diffuse Color Combined on Texture: When color is applied to the texture, the color is blended into the texture when exporting (ver4.2.0). Exclude Ambient Map & Color (Modo): Ambient Map and color are excluded when exporting (ver4.2.0). Save with Alpha Map: Alpha Map is included when exporting (ver4.2.0). Save with Meta Data (*.xml) : Exports garment's pattern(Mesh), physical property and sewing information as Meta Data (ver2.3.0). Diffuse Color Combined on Texture: Combine and save garment's texture image and color as a single image (ver2.2.0). Exclude Ambient Color (for Modo): Exclude Ambient color value when saving materials. ※ Note: #### OBJ Export Updates ### Internal Line(s)/Shape(s) export (including FBX). Thickness export for Quad Mesh. Front, side and back meshes separate export. ### Load as Garment ### Objective Import and simulate OBJ files from other 3D software programs (Maya, 3DS MAX and etc). ### Location Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import (Add) ▶ OBJ to Garment ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import (Add) ▶ OBJ to Garment → Open File window appears. 2. Select a file and click OK. → OBJ to Garment window appears. 3. Set details and click OK. ### Load as Morph Target ### Objective Morph uses two different OBJ files to slowly change object's appearance. Marvelous Designer's default avatars can be modified at Change Avatar Size menu or posed with Show X-Ray Joints function, other 3D software may not have basic Joints set for designed objects, parts may be lost when creating a compatible COLLADA file. As such, this menu can be used to change the object's body type. At least two *.obj files with the same Mesh structure are needed to morph the object. Use this menu to import objects from different 3D software as Avatars, and dress them or change their Poses. ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438235048217) ### Location #### Import OBJ Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ #### Open Morph Target OBJ Import Options Window ▶ Object Type ▶ Load as Morph Target ### Operation 1. Choose two *.obj files to morph. 2. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ → Open File window appears. 3. Select the first file to import and click OK. → Import OBJ window appears. 4. Set details and click OK. 5. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ → Open File window appears. 6. Select the second file to import and click OK. → Open Morph Target window appears. 7. Follow the indicated guideline: OBJ Import Options Window ▶ Object Type ▶ Load as Morph Target 8. Set details and click OK. ※ Note: File name with #(special character) is not going to be loaded. ### Load as Trim ### Objective Use *.obj files designed in other 3D software to organize Trims as well as the Avatars in Garments. When loading a file as an Avatar, the Garment registers the object as an Avatar and allows to drape on top of it, however when the same file is loaded as Trims, the Garment does not register it as an object therefore it passes through it. ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438250539289) ### Location #### OBJ Import Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ #### Import as Scene/Prop OBJ Import Options Window ▶ Object Type ▶ Load as Trim ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ → Open File window appears. 2. Choose file to import and click OK. → Import OBJ window appears. 3. Select Load as Trim in Object Type. 4. Set details and click OK. ### Load as Avatar ### Objective Use *.obj files designed in other 3D software to use as Avatars in Marvelous Designer. When loading a file as an Avatar, the Garment registers the object as an Avatar and allows to drape on top of it. ### Location #### OBJ Import Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ #### Import as Scene/Prop OBJ Import Options Window ▶ Object Type ▶ Load as Avatar ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ → Open File window appears. 2. Choose file to import and click OK. → Import OBJ window appears. 3. Select Load as Avatar in Object Type. 4. Set details and click OK.
content_description: This webpage provides comprehensive guidance on importing and exporting OBJ files in Marvelous Designer, detailing their use in managing Avatars, Garments, and Trims within 3D environments.

content: ### Objective Create ellipse or circle Patterns in the 2D window. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ Ellipse 2D Toolbar ▶ Ellipse ### Operation #### Create 1. Type in the desired values for the options below. Diameter | Set the diameter of the circle Pattern. ---|--- Radius | Set the radius of the circle Pattern (ver3.2.0). Link to maintain the width and height ratio. Circumference | Set the circumference of the circle Pattern (ver3.2.0). ※ Note: Create Pattern Tool Group
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating ellipse and circle patterns in a 2D window using various tools and keyboard shortcuts.

title: Avatar Materials
content: ### Objective Edit avatar color, texture image, and opacity. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Select Avatar ▶ Property Editor ▶ Materials (Selected) ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Select Avatar ▶ Property Editor ▶ Materials (Selected) 2. Adjust individual properties below. Diffuse Color | Sets the color of avatars. ---|--- Diffuse Map | Applies image files on avatar surfaces. The diffuse color overlays on top of the applied image file. Ambient Color | Sets the Ambient Color of avatars. Ambient Map | Applies image files on avatar surfaces. The ambient color overlays on top of the applied image file. Specular Color | Sets the Specular Color of avatars. Specular Map | Applies image files on avatar surfaces. The Specular Color overlays on top of the applied image file. Shininess | Sets the depth of sheen applied to the Specular Color, ranging from soft sheen to plastic-like gloss. Emission Color | Sets the Emission Color of avatars. Opacity | Sets the transparency of avatars. ※Note: Changes made to the Materials (Selected) properties can be saved at Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ Avatar (ver2.5.0). title: ANIMATION MODE: Garment Animation Making
content: ### Objective Tips for creating stable and realistic garment animation for multi-layered garments. ### Operation Optimize 3D Garment for Animation The heavier the garment, the slower and harder it records. Follow the steps below to make it lighter. 1. For a multi-layered garment, increase particle distance to 20mm for inner layers that are not as visible as outer layers. 2. Delete invisible and any other unnecessary layers. 3. Outer layers: →Set the particle distance to 10mm for parts that does not require higher level of expression of wrinkles. →Set the particle distance to 5mm for parts that require higher level of expression of wrinkles. If there is large quantity of layers set to 5mm, set all of them to 7mm. Fix Garment If garment is not fixed to avatar while recording the animation, the garment moves drastically around the avatar due to collision. Certain parts of the garment need to be fixed to the avatar or itself to create more realistic recording. →Use functions such as 'Avatar Tape' or 'Tack on Avatar' to attach shoulder and sides of the garment. →Use 'Tack' function for overlapped layers or any parts that may dangle. Increase Transition Animation Time Increase the transition animation time for heavier garments. In the animation dialogue, enter 5FPS to stabilize the simulation. This makes the avatar movement slower which helps to minimize the collision between the garments. Set Simulation Quality status on 'Complete' for the First Recording Setting Simulation Quality status on 'Complete' minimizes the collision between the avatar and garments. To save time, the simulation quality can be set to 'Normal' for the middle part of the recording as the avatar and garments tend to collide more in the beginning and end. Make sure the simulation to set the quality back on 'Complete' for the end of the Transition Animation. Reevaluate Draping of the Garment after the Recording As the avatar moves, some parts of the garment may collide. When the simulation is off, the 3D garment may appear fine, however there is possibility of unnoticeable collision which may destabilize rest of the recording. →Return to Simulation Mode. ※ Note: From ver2.5.0, it is possible to simulate by pressing the Simulation button without recording it. →Active simulation and make sure the entire garment simulation is stable. →If any parts of the garment is unstable, readjust the layers by using the Select/Move tool. →Once the simulation has been stabilized, go back to the Animation Mode. Set Simulation Quality status on 'Complete' when Recording the Actual Garment Animation Make sure to set Simulation Quality status on 'Complete' for final recordings of Garment Animation as the 'Complete' and the 'Normal' give clearly different results in expressing reality.
content_description: This web page provides essential tips for optimizing 3D garment animation by ensuring realistic and stable movement for multi-layered garments through effective particle distance adjustments and proper attachment techniques.

title: Animation Keyframe and Layer Editing (ver. 12)
content: ## Objective The inclusion of keyframes for simulation caches and keyframe editing tools allow users to fix isolated simulation issues, blend simulations together, adjust timing, and create looping cloth simulation caches. * * * # Edit Animation Keyframes ## Location Animation Editor ▶ Animation Timeline ## Operation 1. Beginning with an avatar with animation, navigate to the Animation Editor. 2. Press the 'Record' button, then stop recording when desired by pressing the 'Record' button again. 3. Select the Animation Layer created for the garment in the Animation Timeline 4. Where vertical lines exist marking Keyframes, select a Keyframe and delete it by pressing the 'Delete' Key. 5. Observe that there is no longer a Keyframe in the previously selected position, and the simulation interpolates vertex positions for the garment linearly across the gap. 6. Where there is now an empty space between Keyframes, move the playtime slider to this position. 7. Select a pattern or garment in the 3D Window. 8. Using the Gizmo, rotate or translate the pattern/garment into a new position. **→** The user can also activate simulation in the 3D Window before creating a new Keyframe. 9. While the playtime slider is still at the position without a keyframe, add a new Keyframe with the 'S' Hotkey. 10. Slide the playtime slider across the area of the timeline where a new frame was keyed, and observe the saved change in the updated frame keyed by the user. **→** To form a smoother transition between the preexisting cache animation and the user-created Keyframe, delete simulation cache Keyframes to the left and right of the user-created Keyframe. ※ Note: Fit the Frame Range \- Click the 'Fit Horizontal' button located next to the 'Animation Max Frame' input field at the bottom right of the Animation Editor. This will display every animation layer from its start to end. \- Double-click the Animation timeslider to switch to the full layer view. (ver.2024.0) * * * # Copy & Paste Keyframes ## Location Animation Editor ▶ Animation Timeline ## Operation 1. Beginning with an avatar with animation, navigate to the Animation Editor. 2. Press the 'Record' button, then stop recording when desired by pressing the 'Record' button again. 3. 'LMB Click' to select a single Keyframe, or 'Shift + LMB Click and Drag' to select multiple Keyframes. **→** If a range of Keyframes has been selected, the user can 'LMB Click and Drag' the white handles on either side of the selection to make fine adjustments. 4. Once the desired selection has been achieved, 'RMB Click' over the highlighted selection to open a pop-up menu then select 'Copy Keyframe' to store the selected frame(s). 5. Move the playtime slider to a different position on the timeline in the same Animation Layer and 'RMB Click' then select 'Paste Keyframe' to past the Keyframe(s) beginning from the current position. ### Animation Editor Keyframe Options: Create Keyframe | 'S' ---|--- Delete Keyframe | 'Del' Copy Keyframe | 'Ctrl+C' Paste Keyframe | 'Ctrl+V' * * * # Cut & Merge Animation Layer ## Location Animation Editor ▶ Animation Timeline ## Operation ### Cut Animation Layer 1. Beginning with an avatar with animation, navigate to the Animation Editor. 2. Press the 'Record' button, then stop recording when desired by pressing the 'Record' button again. 3. Select the resulting Animation Layer by clicking on its title at the left of the Animation Editor interface. 4. Move the playtime slider to a point in the middle of the resulting Animation Layer. 5. Press the 'Cut' button in the Animation Editor Toolbar (scissor icon). 6. Observe that the Animation Layer has split at the current timeline position, and the portion removed has been separated into a new Animation Layer. ### Merge Animation Layers 1. Select two Animation layers by clicking on their titles at the left of the Animation Editor interface while holding the 'Shift' Key. 2. Press the 'Merge' button in the Animation Editor Toolbar (two overlapping squares) to Merge the Animation Layers together. **→** Animation Layers can be moved horizontally (see below) before being merged together to adjust timing. **→** When merging layers, the layers will be merged into the top selected layers. * * * # Animation Layer Controls ## Location Animation Editor ▶ Animation Layer ## Operation ### Move Animation Layer Horizontally 1. Double LMB click on the interpolation space of an Animation Layer (solid pink by default) to activate track movement. 2. When the interpolation space of an Animation Layer is highlighted (red by default), the layer can be moved left and right by clicking and dragging with the mouse cursor. **→** To move the Animation Layer to a specific number of frames, when highlighted, RMB clicks on the Animation layer and select 'Move Layer Horizontally', then enter the desired number of frame units to move the Animation Layer. **→** When highlighted, an Animation Layer can also be moved one frame unit at a time by using the Left or Right Arrow Keys. ### Delete Animation Layer **→** To the left of the Animation Timeline, click on the name of the Animation Layer you would like to delete - highlighting it in grey - and click the "Delete" Key to delete the entire Animation Layer ### Reorder Animation Layer **→** To the left of the Animation Timeline, click on the name of the Animation Layer you would like to move and drag it above or below the Animation Layer. **→** Animation data for an Animation Layer on top will completely block any animation data on an Animation Layer beneath. ### Layer Locking & Keyframe Visibility **→** Lock an Animation Layer by clicking ON the leftmost yellow circle next to the desired Animation Layer's name. **→** Hide an Animation Layer's cached animation by clicking OFF the center yellow circle next to the desired Animation Layer's name. **→** Hide an Animation Layer's keyframe markers by clicking OFF the rightmost yellow circle next to the desired Animation Layer's name. ### Animation Layer Selection **→** To select an Animation Layer, click on its title to the left of the animation timeline (it will turn a lighter shade of grey when selected). **→** To add another Animation Layer to the selection, hold down the 'Shift' Key and click on the title of an additional layer. **→** To remove an Animation Layer from the selection, hold down the 'Ctrl' Key and click on the title of any Animation Layer you would like to deselect. ### Rename Animation layer **→** To rename an animation layer, double-click on its name or right-click on the name of the animation layer and select 'Rename'. **→** Hold down the Shift key to select multiple animation layers, and then follow the above steps to rename them all at once. * * * # Animation Editor UI Updates ## Location Animation Editor ▶ Animation Editor Toolbar ## Operation ### Animation Editor Icon Additions & Updates: Loop | Circular Arrow | **→** Sets animation timeline playback to loop. ---|---|--- Playback Speed | 1X | **→** Ranges from 1/4X to 8X speed. Merge Selected Animation Layers | Two Overlapping Squares | **→** Merge selected Animation Layers into a single layer. Cut Selected Animation Layer | Scissors | **→** Split Animation Layer at current timeline position. Delete | Trash Can | **→** Deletes Animation Layer or Keyframe depending on selection. Create Keyframe | I | **→** Creates new Keyframe at current timeline position. * * *
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide users with comprehensive tools and instructions for editing animation keyframes, enabling them to resolve simulation issues, blend animations, and enhance their cloth simulations efficiently.

title: Line Tack on Garment
content: ### Objective Create lines on Garment and tack to each other by lines / shapes. (Ver. MD7) ### Location 3D window tool bar Line tack tool ### Operation 1. Select the tool according to the Location above. 2. Mouse over to a garment from 3D window. Point follows mouse cursor. 3. Double click on the garment where want to create start point of line / shape. Double click to complete the line / shape Double click on start point of line to create closed shape. 4. Create second line/ shape. Once all the two lines / shapes have been created, connection line for line / shape will be displayed. 5. Click the simulation button. Two lines/ shapes tack to each other along the connection line. * During the creation of the line, pressing the Shift key will display the front, back, side center line and guide line of last point. * Press the Ctrl key to create curved line. * When creating a line, can cancel it from the last point by pressing the Delete key on Keyboard. Press the Esc / Ctrl+Z to cancel the whole point.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for using the Line Tack Tool in the 3D window to create and connect lines and shapes on garments.

Select a Topstitch with Edit Topstitch tool in the 2D window for changing its properties. → Topstitch properties appear on the Property Editor. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Topstitch Property Editor ▶ Extend Start / Extend End

title: Custom View
content: ### Objective Easily open and save custom view of the 3D window at your convenience. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Viewpoint ▶ Custom View Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) ▶ Custom View ### Operation #### Create 1. Rotate the 3D Window as desired. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Viewpoint ▶ Custom View Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) ▶ Custom View →The Custom View window appears. 3. Left click on the camera icon on the right top corner. → The current view is saved and added to the Custom View window. 4. Double click on the added custom view. → The 3D Window rotates automatically to reflect the custom view. #### Open/Save 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Viewpoint ▶ Custom View Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) ▶ Custom View → The Custom View window appears. 2. Add the desired custom view. 3. Click on the Open or the Save All button. → The group of custom views is opened or saved. #### Delete 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Viewpoint ▶ Custom View Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) ▶ Custom View → The Custom View window appears. 2. Add the desired custom view. 3. Right-click on the custom view to be deleted. →The right-click pop-up menu appears. 4. Select Delete. → The selected custom view is deleted from the Custom View window. #### Rename 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Viewpoint ▶ Custom View Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) ▶ Custom View → The Custom View window appears. 2. Add the desired custom view. 3. Right click on the custom view to be deleted. →The right click pop-up menu appears. 4. Select Rename. → Edit the name as the custom view's name field is activated. ※ Note: Starting from ver4.1.0, Delete All or Overwrite custom views using the right-click pop-up menu.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for users to easily create, save, open, delete, and rename custom views of the 3D window for enhanced convenience and personalization.

title: Flatten
content: ### Objective Extract Patterns based on lines and shapes created on an Avatar. ※ Note: The Flattening function only extracts closed shapes as Patterns. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Flatten 3D Toolbar ▶ Flatten ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Flatten 3D Toolbar ▶ Flatten → Points no longer appear and only lines appear on the Avatar. 2. Hover the mouse over the shape to be extracted as a Pattern. → The area to be flattened appears in light blue. 3. Select all areas to be extracted by holding Shift on the keyboard, then clicking on the desired areas. → The selected areas are highlighted in yellow. 4. Press the Enter key to execute **Flatten (Separate)**. → The selected areas on the Avatar are converted to patterns and appear in both the 3D and 2D windows. → The default Fabric is applied to all Patterns created with the Flatten tool. → Sewing lines are automatically established for adjacent Patterns. → The lines remain on the Avatar. 5. Press the Shift + Enter key to execute **Flatten (Merge)**. → If adjacent surfaces are selected, a single merged pattern will be created.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for extracting and creating patterns from an Avatar using the Flatten tool in a 3D garment design application.

title: MODULAR MODE: General Process of Using Modular Mode
content: Follow the procedure of the Modular Mode to build and design with your own Pattern database. To build the Pattern database, take following procedures: Open Modular Template ▶ Add Patterns or Garments ▶ Drag the Patterns into Block Boxes ▶ Sew the Patterns and the Block Boxes ▶ Save it as a Block file (If there is no Modular file in a folder where the Blocks are being saved, save a Modular file too)
content_description: Discover how to create and customize your own Pattern database using the Modular Mode by following our step-by-step procedure.

title: Create 2D Graphic Measurement
content: ### Objective View graphic position from the Pattern outline with 2D measurements. (ver2.5.0) ### Location Graphics ▶ Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurement ### Operation 1. 2D Toolbar ▶Select a graphic with Transform Graphic. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Graphics ▶ Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurement 3. Select the desired 2D measurement option. To Center | View the 2D measurements from the center of the graphic to left/right/top/bottom of the Pattern outline. ---|--- To Outline | View the 2D measurements from the left/right/top/bottom of the graphic to the Pattern outline. → The 2D measurements are now being displayed accordingly.

title: Lock Remesh Patterns
content: ### Objective Lock patterns from selection based on whether or not they are dynamic Marvelous Designer patterns with adjustable particle distance and curve points, or remeshed patterns created with the Topology Tools & Remesh All. * * * ### Location 2D Pattern Window ▶ Lock Pattern Drop-down Menu ▶ Lock All Remesh Patterns ### Operation 1. Load a garment. 2. Create topology with the 'Create Topology' Tool in the 2D Pattern Window. 3. When complete, with blue retopology still visible, Right Mouse Button Click in the 2D Pattern Window then select 'Remesh All (duplicate)'. → Retopology meshes are placed directly on top of the original patterns. 4. Click on 'Lock All Remesh Patterns' in the Lock Pattern drop-down menu within the 2D Window to lock all remeshed patterns from selection. → Click and move original patterns as desired with the 'Transform Pattern' Tool. → Click on 'Unlock All Remesh Patterns' to release the selection mask. 5. Click on 'Lock All Pattern Outlines' and 'Lock All Internal Lines' to lock original patterns from selection. → Click and move remeshed patterns as desired with the 'Transform Pattern' Tool.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step guidance on locking and managing remesh patterns in Marvelous Designer to streamline garment design and editing processes.

title: Curved Side Geometry
content: ### Objective Apply and adjust curvature on edges of Patterns for more natural and realistic look (ver2.2.0). ### Location 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern ### Operation 1. Firstly, change the 3D Garment rendering style to Thick Textured Surface in the 3D window. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 3. Select a Pattern or Pattern line to express curved sided effect. → Its properties appear in the Property Editor. 4. Enter a desired value at: Property Editor ▶ Selected Line ▶ Curved Side Geometry ▶ Curvature (%) → The curvature is now being applied according to the entered value. ※ Note: The maximum Curvature (%) value is 50 percent (%) of the fabric thickness. For instance, if the fabric thickness is being set at 1mm, the maximum Curvature (%) is 0.5mm.
content_description: Learn how to apply and adjust curvature on pattern edges for a more natural and realistic appearance using the 2D Toolbar in version 2.2.0.

title: Free Topstitch
content: ### Objective Create a Topstitch to freely sew regardless of the points of Pattern or Internal Shape. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Topstitch ▶ Free Topstitch 2D Toolbar ▶ Free Topstitch ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Topstitch ▶ Free Topstitch 2D Toolbar ▶ Free Topstitch 2. Click on a point where a Topstitch begins. 3. Move mouse to the direction where the Topstitch is going to be created. → The selected area appears in red color. 4. Click on another point where the Topstitch ends. → The tTopstitch is now created with being highlighted. ※ Note: * Click-and-drag in the 2D window to encompass all segments where Topstitches to be applied. Topstitches appear on all selected segments (ver3.2.0). * Use lasso selection to select Pattern Outlines and Internal Lines where Topstitches should be created on (ver3.2.0). * OBJ Topstitches temporarily disappear when the Simulation is activated, but they appear again when the Simulation is deactivated (ver3.2.0). * Right click when creating the Topstitch to enter specific length (ver4.2.0).
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for using the Free Topstitch feature in the 2D Toolbar, enabling users to create custom Topstitches on patterns and shapes effortlessly.

title: Trace as / Convert to Internal Shape
content: ### Objective Use the Trace function to convert selected lines/shapes or areas into Internal Lines/Shapes. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Line (3D Pattern) ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Line (3D Pattern) 2. Click on created Baselines or Internal Lines on 3D Garment. → The selected Baselines or Internal Lines are now highlighted in yellow. 3.
